name: work_plan
title: Work plan: batch a dependency graph
description: Work plan: turn a dependency graph you hand it into the batches that may run in parallel — pure computation over `nodes`: no file opened, no path taken, nothing mutated. Use it when the graph is in your hands (tasks with depends_on); use shiftwork_plan when the graph is a shift-work checkpoint on disk, which it reads for you under the same batching rules. Batch k holds every node whose dependencies all sit in batches below k; `sequence` is the batches flattened; `width` is the largest batch — the fan-out an orchestrator must afford. Inside a batch: priority descending, then the order the nodes were given; both halves are contract, so two implementations answer byte-identically. Empty `nodes` is an ANSWER (no batches, width 0), not a refusal. Four refusals, in this order, one sentence each: `nodes[<i>].<field> must be ...` (an id that is not a string, depends_on not a list of strings, priority not an integer — named by position, never coerced), `duplicate node id <id>`, `node <id> depends on <dep>, which no node declares`, and `the graph has a cycle: <a> -> <b> -> <a>`. It reports what the graph PERMITS and decides nothing about what is safe to dispatch together: `depends_on` encodes logical order, not file contention.

nodes.title: Nodes

depends_on.description: Ids this node waits for; every one of them must be declared by some node. Optional: absent or null means none

priority.description: Tie-break inside a batch, descending. Optional; 0 when absent

nodes.description: The graph: one object per task, {id, depends_on?, priority?}. The order given is the tie-break inside a batch after priority.

result.description: `plan` on success; `error` with `reason` for one of the four refusals.

batches.description: Node ids by wave: batch k holds every node whose dependencies all sit in batches below k.

width.description: The largest batch length: the widest fan-out.

reason.description: With result `error`: one sentence saying why the call was refused.
